mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 207 1.4 or 1.6 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.4 or 1.6 engine typically costs £650-£1,750 supply-only, depending on fuel type and power output. 1.4 HDi units start around £650, 1.6 HDi units from £750, 1.4 VTi from £800 and 1.6 VTi from £950. Used engines start from £550. Supply & fit adds £450-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £3,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 207 1.6 VTi engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 207 1.6 VTi (EP6) engine problems are timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle, water pump bearing seizure leading to overheating, and VANOS solenoid clogging affecting valve timing. Ignoring the cold-start rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi anti-pollution fault?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 'Anti-Pollution Fault' warning on a Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi is usually caused by DPF blockage from short-journey driving preventing regeneration, or EGR valve carbon buildup. The warning often appears alongside loss of power and limp mode.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 207 1.4 or 1.6?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 207 1.4 or 1.6 engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 207 values typically £800-£3,000, a rebuilt engine at £650-£1,750 represents a significant but often justifiable investment. For sub-£1,500 examples, a used engine from £550 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi (9HX/9HZ) engine typically reaches 120,000-150,000 miles. Regular oil changes, DPF-friendly driving (regular motorway runs) and timely turbo maintenance are essential for longevity. The 1.4 HDi is similarly durable but requires strict timing belt intervals.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 207 HDi and VTi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peugeot 207 HDi engines (8HZ, 9HX, 9HZ) are diesel units offering superior fuel economy (50+ mpg) and strong torque for motorway driving, but require DPF and EGR maintenance. VTi engines (EP3, EP6) are petrol units with smoother, higher-revving characteristics but are prone to timing chain issues. Choose diesel for high-mileage motorway use; petrol for shorter urban trips.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 207 1.4 & 1.6 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 207 1.4 and 1.6 engines powered the vast majority of UK 207s across its 2006-2014 production run. The range combined PSA's durable DV4 and DV6 diesel families with the BMW-developed Prince petrol engines (EP3 and EP6), offering buyers a choice between economical diesel commuters and refined petrol hatchbacks. The 1.4 HDi (8HZ) delivered exceptional fuel economy, while the 1.6 HDi (9HX/9HZ) became the UK's volume diesel choice. On the petrol side, the 1.4 VTi (EP3) and 1.6 VTi (EP6) replaced older TU units with modern variable valve timing - but introduced the notorious timing chain vulnerabilities that continue to drive replacement enquiries today.

milestones.description: **2006** - 207 launched with 1.4 HDi (8HZ, 70hp) and 1.6 HDi 90 (9HX, 90hp) diesel engines
**2007** - 1.6 HDi 110 (9HZ, 110hp) introduced for GT and SW models; 1.4 VTi (EP3, 95hp) and 1.6 VTi (EP6, 120hp) petrol engines launched, replacing TU series
**2008** - 1.6 THP (EP6DT, 150hp) added for GT and Sport trims
**2009** - 1.6 THP RC (5FY, 175hp) introduced for performance variants; CC convertible launched
**2010** - Revised EGR and DPF calibration on HDi units; updated piston rings on EP3 to reduce oil consumption
**2013** - Final production year for 207 in UK; 208 takes over

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 8HZ, 9HX, 9HZ, EP3 and EP6 engine fitted to the Peugeot 207 1.4 and 1.6 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 207 1.4 & 1.6 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 207 1.4 and 1.6 engine lineup is heavily shaped by PSA's DV4/DV6 diesel and Prince EP3/EP6 petrol families, both of which carry well-documented failure patterns that frequently drive replacement enquiries. Diesel owners commonly face turbo and injector degradation, while VTi petrol models are notorious for timing chain stretch. Every rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.4 and 1.6 engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.6 VTi Engines Rattle and Fail
problems.rootCause: The rear-mounted timing chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch and skip teeth on the cam sprockets. Cold-start rattling is the first warning sign - ignoring it can lead to valve-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, tensioner, guides and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Reliable for 60k+ miles if caught before jump

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt EP6 with upgraded tensioner

problems.recommendation: If you hear a cold-start rattle above 50k miles, address the chain immediately. Once the chain jumps, valve damage is almost guaranteed, making full replacement the only economical option on a 207 valued under £2,500.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6 Peugeot 207 1.6 VTi engine prices

problems.h4: Turbo Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi Engines Lose Boost
problems.rootCause: Oil starvation and carbon buildup on the turbo actuator arm cause sticking vanes and eventual compressor blade fatigue. Owners report loss of power, black smoke and limp mode activation.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo removal, actuator calibration, carbon clean
repairOptions.longevity: Short-term fix only if blades are undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full DV6 rebuild with upgraded turbo and oil pump
repairOptions.longevity: Eliminates downstream bearing damage from metal shards

problems.recommendation: On high-mileage Peugeot 207 HDi units, a failing turbo usually indicates broader oil circulation issues. Replacing just the turbo rarely prevents recurrence; a fully rebuilt engine with corrected oil galleries offers the only long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Find reconditioned 9HZ Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi engines with warranty

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi Engines Run Rough
problems.rootCause: Piezo injector seals degrade under high thermal load, allowing combustion gases to leak and carbonise around the injector seat. Symptoms include rough idle, black smoke and reduced power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove, test, replace faulty injectors, code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if only one injector has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt DV6 with fresh injector harness and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended when multiple injectors fail or head seats are damaged

problems.recommendation: If you experience rough idle and black smoke after 80k miles, get injector coding checked first. However, if cylinder head damage is confirmed from gas leakage, a rebuilt engine is significantly cheaper than head milling plus four new injectors.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for Peugeot 207 diesel injector and engine replacement

problems.h4: DPF Blockage - Why Peugeot 207 1.6 HDi Triggers Anti-Pollution Faults
problems.rootCause: Frequent short trips prevent DPF regeneration cycles, causing soot and oil ash to solidify in the filter substrate. The famous "Anti-Pollution Fault" warning is the first sign of trouble.

repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix if filter isn't physically cracked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuilt DV6 with EGR/DPF components refreshed
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for urban drivers with chronic regeneration failure

problems.recommendation: DPF blockage on the Peugeot 207 rarely happens in isolation - it usually points to EGR faults or turbo oil burn. For city-dwelling owners, a rebuilt engine with refreshed emissions components offers better long-term reliability than repeated DPF replacements.
problems.cta: -> Compare Peugeot 207 HDi engine prices with DPF solutions

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - Why Peugeot 207 1.4 VTi Engines Burn Oil
problems.rootCause: Piston ring wear allows oil to seep into the combustion chamber, causing blue smoke and high oil consumption. Peugeot revised the piston ring design in later production to address this issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine removal, piston ring replacement, cylinder honing
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if cylinder walls are not scored

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded piston rings
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended when oil consumption exceeds 1 litre per 1,000 miles

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 207 1.4 VTi is consuming more than 1 litre per 1,000 miles, the piston rings are likely compromised. A full rebuilt engine with upgraded rings is often more cost-effective than a partial rebuild.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP3 Peugeot 207 1.4 VTi engine prices
